learning_outcomes.text: Understand sorting and search algorithms appropriate to computational solutions
Identify, rewrite and review common ways of organizing data and associated algorithms (with and without dynamic memory management, with iterative or recursive algorithms)
Estimate and value the complexity of algorithms on alternative data structures
Prototype new forms of organization of data and associated algorithms suited to solve new computational problems

assessment_rules: Assessment throughout the semester: 10 individual programming exercises (25%), without a minimum grade. Two written tests (75%), each with a minimum grade of 7.5 points. Alternatively, an individual final exam (100%) can be taken in the 1st, 2nd, or Special Season.
bibliography: R. Sedgewick and K. Wayne, Algorithms, 4th edition, Addison-Wesley, 2012
D. Harel, Algorithmics: the Spirit of Computing, 3th edition, Addison-Wesley, 2004
F. Santos and C. Conti, Algoritmos e Estruturas de Dados - Exercícios, ISCTE-IUL, 2022.
